Subject: Performance MAP: throughput & unit-econ targets (FinLedger)

Kimberly —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As discussed on the call, FinLedger wants to capture the performance guarantees and acceptance criteria in a short Mutual Action Plan so procurement can move the commercial review along. I attached our initial MAP spreadsheet (FinLedger_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a redline SOW for context.

High level asks from our side:
- Sustained throughput target: support 18 sustained QPS for our primary checkout path (avg payload ~420 tokens / request).
- TTFT <= 250ms for first token under standard P95 conditions.
- Concurrency: up to 24 concurrent sessions during peak windows.
- Clear unit economics: cost per 1M tokens (broken out by generation vs embeddings), and an assumed tokenization model so we can translate to monthly spend.

Can Redwood provide a short evaluation plan (test harness, timeline, milestone acceptance criteria) and a simple cost model we can plug into procurement? We’re hoping for a 2–3 week evaluation window starting next week.

Appreciate it — copying Procurement to keep timing visible.

Regards,
Alex Chen
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
FinLedger

Subject: Re: Performance MAP: throughput & unit-econ targets (FinLedger)

Alex —

Thanks for the concise ask, and for sharing the MAP spreadsheet. I’ve sketched a proposed evaluation plan below that we can fold directly into your FinLedger_MAP_v1.xlsx as milestones. I’ve also attached a compact benchmark matrix we’ll use to capture tokens/sec and sustained QPS across the traffic profiles you mentioned (redwood_benchmark_matrix.csv).

Proposed evaluation plan (2-week focused sprint):
1) Week 0 — Test prep (3 days): share test harness instructions, dataset subset, and generate baseline run with your sample payloads.
2) Week 1 — Throughput & TTFT runs (5 days):
   - Sustained QPS sweeps at 6, 12, 18 QPS.
   - Measure tokens/sec (tail and mean), per-run TTFT (first token latency) at P50/P95/P99.
   - Concurrency scale test up to 24 sessions.
   - Capture KV-cache hit assumptions for chat flows.
3) Week 2 — Costing & acceptance (4 days):
   - Run steady-state 12-hour sustained load for economic extrapolation.
   - Produce unit economics: cost/1M tokens (generation), cost/1M tokens (embeddings), and expected spend at your projected monthly token volume.
   - Review results, document acceptance criteria in the MAP and confirm signature.

Acceptance criteria (recommended):
- Sustained 18 QPS with TTFT P95 <= 300ms and P50 <= 180ms (we’ll aim for your 250ms P95 target; will validate on first runs).
- Tokens/sec for peak profile >= 125k tokens/sec across the pool (aggregate).
- Unit-econ projection within 15% of target rate (so procurement has a bounded estimate).

Operational notes:
- We’ll use a small dedicated test pool (Redwood dedicated preview) with the same quantization and batching config we recommend for production.
- If we see a regression in quality vs your prompts during the run, we’ll pause and do a quick model profile adjustment rather than pushing past acceptance criteria.

Next steps:
- Alex: confirm you’re good with the 2-week window starting Mon 15 Mar (we’ll reserve test capacity).
- Ben: can you share the test harness link and a short runbook for FinLedger engineers to kick off?
- Marissa: I’ll need a short one-pager on unit-econ assumptions (GPU cost, amortization, expected batch sizes) to drop into the MAP.

Thanks — will turn this into a milestoned MAP row once we have confirmation.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On the scheduling front I can confirm the test harness is ready. Link and creds below (test cluster: redwood-eval-ff). We’ll provide a small reference dataset and a dockerized load-generator with your payload profile.

Test harness link: https://internal.redwood.ai/eval/redwood-eval-ff (access will be provisioned to Alex and procurement contact).
Runbook highlights:
- Step 1: Clone the repo, run generate_payloads.sh with your sample csv (we’ll provide).
- Step 2: Start the harness pointing at the redwood-eval endpoint (we’ll give a temp API key).
- Step 3: Use the benchmark matrix to log tokens/sec and latency buckets for each run.

I recommend starting with a 2-full-day sanity run at 6 QPS to validate instrumentation, then ramp to 18 QPS over two days. If all good, do the 12-hour steady-state run in Week 2.
